record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the class 2DPDA of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata exactly equal to DLBA, the class of languages accepted by deterministic linear bounded automata?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let 2DPDA denote the class of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata: machines equipped with a read-only input tape (with end markers) on which a single head may move in both directions, together with a deterministic pushdown stack, that accept by entering a designated accepting state. Let DLBA denote the class of languages accepted by deterministic linear bounded automata: deterministic Turing machines whose work tape is restricted to the cells originally occupied by the input (equivalently, deterministic nondeterministic-space O(n) machines restricted to be deterministic, i.e., DSPACE(n)).

Determine whether these two classes are equal:
$$ \mathrm{2DPDA} \stackrel{?}{=} \mathrm{DLBA}. $$
That is, prove or disprove that a language is accepted by some one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automaton if and only if it is accepted by some deterministic linear bounded automaton.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether 2DPDA equals DLBA appears to remain open. 2DPDA is known to be contained in DTIME(n) (Cook's theorem) and hence in DLBA, but no proof of equality or separation has been reported. Subsequent literature on 2DPDA simulations (e.g., revisitings of Cook's simulation) does not claim to have resolved this containment-versus-equality question.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in the theory of computation as questions about two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces major open problems in computation theory to questions about 2DPDA languages, listing 2DPDA = DLBA as one such open question.
status_evidence.claim: The equality 2DPDA = DLBA is posed as an open problem reducing other major open questions in complexity theory.

status_evidence.title: Simulation of Two-Way Pushdown Automata Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Revisits Cook's linear-time simulation of 2DPDA but does not establish 2DPDA = DLBA.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on simulating 2DPDA does not resolve the 2DPDA vs DLBA question.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic two-way one-head pushdown automata are very powerful
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates surprising power of 2DPDA but does not equate the class with DLBA.
status_evidence.claim: Power-of-2DPDA results in the literature stop short of proving 2DPDA = DLBA.
